thread:
Allison Grant: heads up — I’m putting together the quant perf dashboard panels this afternoon (FP8/INT8). Need quick alignment on tag conventions + alert routing. Goal is: panels slice by model/GPU/quant mode + we can route regressions to #eng-runtime.

Aisha Bello: +1. We should be careful about label cardinality though. What dimensions are we committing to?

Allison Grant: draft dimensions I’m planning to use (from benchmark artifacts + runtime spans):
- `model_family` (llama/qwen/mistral)
- `model_id` (exact hosted model name)
- `gpu_sku` (A100/H100/H200/L40S)
- `quant_mode` (fp16/fp8/int8)
- `phase` (prefill/decode/e2e)
- `workload_preset` (ex: chat_streaming_default, chat_nostreaming_default)
- `runtime_version` (release train version string)
Maybe also `kernel_family` but I’m worried it’ll explode.

Sean Gallagher: kernel_family / kernel_id is going to murder us in Prometheus if it’s a label. If you need it, keep it in logs/traces and only show “top N” via log-derived panels.

Julian Moore: +1. For the runtime spans I just landed (kernel-selection), we can emit `kernel_id` + shapes but I wouldn’t want that in metrics labels. Suggest:
- metrics labels: only stable dims (gpu_sku/model_family/quant_mode/phase/runtime_version)
- logs/traces: kernel_id, shapes, chosen algo, etc

Noah Patel: agree. We mainly need kernel_id for attribution when something regresses. Dashboard should answer “is it real + which phase + which GPUs” quickly, then link to traces for the kernel-level details.

Rina Kobayashi: benchmark harness artifacts already have these tags baked in:
- `model`
- `gpu`
- `quant_mode`
- `runtime_commit`
- `preset`
- `scheduler_policy`
We can map those to the stable set above. For `scheduler_policy`, we might want it for the experiment matrix but shouldn’t be default view.

Aisha Bello: what’s the plan for alerting? We shouldn’t page SRE on these; seems like a “notify runtime team” thing.

Allison Grant: yep, alerts will go to #eng-runtime only (no paging). I’ll set them as “warning” style + include links to the run + comparator diff.

Connor O'Brien: please route to #eng-runtime and tag me + @here only if it’s release-blocking. For canary failures, we need a single message that includes: baseline version, candidate version, metric deltas, and whether allowlisted.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to not paging. Also, we should name alerts so they’re easy to grep. Something like `quant-perf-regression/{metric}/{gpu}/{model_family}`.

Marcus Reed: what exact metrics are we surfacing? The runtime folks keep debating TTFT vs TPOT vs throughput.

Allison Grant: panels I’m proposing (per GPU SKU, with quant_mode selector):
1) TTFT p50/p95 (streaming chat)
2) TPOT p50/p95 (streaming chat)
3) tokens/sec (decode throughput) for non-streaming batch
4) queue wait p95 split by phase (needs Julian’s scheduler histograms)
5) error rate / fallback rate (quant path fallback to fp16)
Plus a “regression table” panel: latest run vs previous green run.

Noah Patel: that’s good. Please include both absolute and % change in the regression table. TTFT can move in ms but % tells the story.

Rina Kobayashi: for the regression table, easiest is using the results JSON pushed by benchmark-lab. It has `ttft_ms_p95`, `tpot_ms_p95`, `tokens_per_s`, and `prefill_ms`, `decode_ms` breakdown.

Aisha Bello: if it’s from results JSON, are we putting it into Prometheus or into Grafana via Loki/Parquet?

Allison Grant: current plan:
- store artifacts in GCS
- ingest “summary metrics” into Prometheus (low cardinality)
- keep per-run detailed stuff in parquet (queried by the report generator)
Grafana panels will be Prometheus for time series + a linkout to the full run report.

Sean Gallagher: ok. Re: tag conventions, for Prometheus labels, I’d strongly prefer:
- `model_family`
- `gpu_sku`
- `quant_mode`
- `phase`
- `preset`
- `runtime_version`
Avoid `runtime_commit` if it changes every run; map commit -> version string if you can.

Julian Moore: FYI, my metrics are currently emitted as:
- `redwood_runtime_queue_wait_ms_bucket{quant_mode,phase,gpu_sku}`
- `redwood_runtime_batch_size{quant_mode,phase,gpu_sku}`
No model labels there (by design). But benchmark runs are isolated per model anyway, so you can correlate by run metadata.

Allison Grant: makes sense. For the benchmark-derived metrics, I can keep model_family + maybe model_id. But we can default the dashboard to model_family to keep it sane.

Aisha Bello: what about region? perf lab is mostly us-west-2 but sometimes we run in eu-central.

Sean Gallagher: region label is ok (small set). Add `region` but keep it optional.

Connor O'Brien: +1 region. We had a false alarm last month because the “baseline” ran in a different region node pool.

Allison Grant: ok, adding `region`.

Marcus Reed: can we also get an alert on “fallback rate”? INT8 falling back to FP16 can look like perf improvement/regression depending on which path was used.

Noah Patel: yes please. A perf regression without knowing fallback rate is basically useless.

Allison Grant: noted. I’ll add a panel + alert: `quant_fallback_rate > 0.5%` for canary runs (tunable).

Aisha Bello: thresholds — are we using the draft regression thresholds doc? (blocking vs non-blocking)

Connor O'Brien: yes, use the quant regression thresholds policy. For now: warn at 3% regression, “block” at 5% for primary metrics, unless allowlisted. (we can refine after a week of data)

Allison Grant: cool. Alert routing plan:
- Grafana Alerting -> Slack contact point “eng-runtime”
- alerts land in #eng-runtime with title `quant-perf-regression` and include labels gpu_sku/model_family/quant_mode/phase + delta
- no pager

Sean Gallagher: please also add a note in the alert that perf-lab contention can cause noise, and link to the runbook section on reruns. We’ve already had folks chasing ghosts.

Allison Grant: will do.

Grafana Bot: Allison Grant created dashboard "Quant Perf (FP8/INT8)" (folder: Serving Runtime). Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/quant-perf-fp8-int8

Allison Grant: dashboard is up in draft. Can someone sanity check the label names before I wire alerts?

Rina Kobayashi: looking now. I see `gpu` not `gpu_sku` on a couple panels.

Allison Grant: ugh good catch. I’ll normalize to `gpu_sku` everywhere.

Julian Moore: and `quant` should be `quant_mode` (consistency with runtime metrics). Otherwise it’s annoying to template.

Allison Grant: updated.

Aisha Bello: reviewed. Looks good. One more ask: add a “latest runtime version” annotation on charts so it’s obvious when we switched trains.

Allison Grant: yep, I can add annotations for `runtime_version` change events.

Connor O'Brien: once alerts are on, can you ensure they tag #eng-runtime and not #eng-sre? We want the kernel/scheduler folks to see it first.

Allison Grant: confirmed. I’ll also add a dashboard link in the pinned items for #eng-runtime once it’s stable.

Sean Gallagher: action items:
- Allison: normalize labels + add fallback panels + wire slack contact point
- Rina: confirm benchmark exporter emits `runtime_version` and `region`
- Connor: paste the exact threshold table you want in the alert description so we’re aligned

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: I’ll ship the alert rules by EOD and post a test alert to #eng-runtime for verification.
